Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: customer-service-reply
Version: 1.0.2

The skill bundle is a legitimate customer service template generator. The core logic in `scripts/cs.sh` is a Python script that takes user input and prints pre-defined response templates for various e-commerce scenarios (refunds, complaints, FAQs). There is no evidence of network activity, file system access, data exfiltration, or malicious prompt injection.

llm.guidance: This skill appears coherent and self-contained: it prints canned customer-service replies locally and does not ask for credentials or network access. Before installing or running: 1) Open SKILL.md and scripts/cs.sh in a text editor that shows invisible characters (or run hexdump -C SKILL.md) to inspect the flagged unicode control characters. 2) Review scripts/cs.sh (you can read the whole embedded Python) to confirm there are no calls to os.system, subprocess that contact external hosts, or file writes you don't expect. 3) If you will run it, do so as a non-privileged user and, if concerned, run it in a sandbox/VM. 4) If you plan to use generated templates with real customer data, ensure you do not paste sensitive customer credentials into prompts — the tool does not transmit data externally, but it's best practice to avoid mixing private data with third-party tools. If you want, paste the full SKILL.md contents here and I can highlight any invisible/control characters and re-check the script for hidden behaviors.
llm.findings: [unicode-control-chars] unexpected: The static pre-scan found unicode control characters in SKILL.md. This is not expected for a simple README/instruction file. It may be harmless formatting (zero-width spaces or Invisibles) but could also be an attempt to hide injected instructions; review SKILL.md for invisible characters (use hexdump, cat -v, or an editor that shows invisibles).
